answer: Practically, the chain should make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because raven only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any river approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
